title: Quick Reads: Small Discoveries
level_note: Original short-passage comprehension practice informed by broad Fountas & Pinnell Level L context. Not an official benchmark assessment.

passages.title: The Red Scarf
passages.text: Mina found a red scarf on the playground after lunch. She carried it to the office, but no one had asked for it. The next morning, she saw Jay looking under the swings. “I lost my scarf,” he said. Mina showed him the lost-and-found box. Jay's face brightened when he spotted the red scarf inside. “I thought the wind took it,” he said. Mina smiled. The wind had moved the scarf, but a careful friend had helped it find its way home.

passages.title: Busy Bees
passages.text: A bee visits a flower to find nectar, a sweet liquid. As the bee moves from flower to flower, tiny grains of pollen stick to its body. Some pollen rubs off on the next flower. This helps the plant make seeds. Bees do not carry pollen because they are trying to help plants. They are looking for food. Still, the bee and the flower both benefit from the visit.

passages.title: The Chalk Arrow
passages.text: After the rain, Lila saw a chalk arrow on the sidewalk. It pointed toward the park gate. Beside it lay a damp paper bag with a bright green handle. Lila followed the arrows and found two more. At the last arrow, a little boy was searching the grass. “My lunch bag!” he cried. Lila handed it to him. “I made arrows so I could find my way back,” he said. The rain had washed away the first mark, but not every clue.

questions.question_text: Where did Mina find the scarf?
questions.explanation: The passage says Mina found the scarf on the playground after lunch.

questions.question_text: What was Jay doing the next morning?
questions.explanation: Mina sees Jay looking under the swings before he tells her he lost his scarf.

questions.question_text: Jay “spotted” the red scarf. What does spotted mean here?
questions.explanation: Jay sees the scarf in the box, so spotted means noticed or saw it.

questions.question_text: How did Jay probably feel when he saw the scarf?
questions.explanation: Jay's face brightens when he finds his lost scarf, which suggests he is glad to have it back.

questions.question_text: Which idea best fits this passage?
choices: Mina helps Jay find something he lost.
Jay teaches Mina how to play on the swings.
The wind carries Mina's lunch to the office.
Lila draws a map of the playground.
questions.correct_answer: Mina helps Jay find something he lost.
questions.explanation: The events are about Mina finding the scarf and helping Jay recognize it.

questions.question_text: What sweet liquid does a bee look for in a flower?
questions.explanation: The first sentence says a bee visits a flower to find nectar.

questions.question_text: What happens after pollen sticks to a bee?
choices: Some pollen rubs off on another flower.
The bee turns the pollen into nectar.
The flower carries the bee to its hive.
The pollen falls into the bee's nest.
questions.correct_answer: Some pollen rubs off on another flower.
questions.explanation: The passage explains that pollen sticks to the bee and then rubs off on the next flower.

questions.question_text: The bee and flower both “benefit.” What does benefit mean?
questions.explanation: The bee gets food, and pollen helps the plant make seeds, so each gets something useful.

questions.question_text: Why does the passage say both the bee and flower benefit?
choices: The bee finds food, and the flower can make seeds.
The bee makes a home inside each flower.
The flower keeps the bee warm at night.
The bee gives the flower its sweet nectar.
questions.correct_answer: The bee finds food, and the flower can make seeds.
questions.explanation: The bee gathers nectar for food, while moving pollen helps the plant make seeds.

questions.question_text: What is this short text mostly about?
choices: How bees and flowers help one another
How bees build a nest in a tree
Why flowers close when it rains
questions.correct_answer: How bees and flowers help one another
questions.explanation: The text describes how bees get nectar and how pollen helps plants make seeds.

questions.question_text: What did Lila see on the sidewalk?
questions.explanation: The passage begins with Lila noticing a chalk arrow after the rain.

questions.question_text: What was the little boy trying to find?
questions.explanation: The boy calls out when Lila hands him the lunch bag.

questions.question_text: What did Lila do after she saw the first arrow?
choices: She drew a picture of the rain.
questions.explanation: Lila follows the first arrow and then finds two more along the way.

questions.question_text: Why had the boy made arrows?
choices: So he could find his way back
So he could lead bees to flowers
So he could mark a place to play
So he could show Lila where to eat
questions.correct_answer: So he could find his way back
questions.explanation: The boy says he made arrows to help him find his way back.

questions.question_text: Which sentence best tells what happened?
choices: Lila follows chalk clues and helps a boy find his lunch bag.
Lila teaches a boy how to draw paper cranes.
A boy finds a scarf beside the school swings.
Rain washes every clue away before Lila can help.
questions.correct_answer: Lila follows chalk clues and helps a boy find his lunch bag.
questions.explanation: Lila follows the remaining arrows and finds the boy searching for his lunch bag.
